ruled_out.hypothesis: C1: FullMath.mulDiv phantom overflow at max inputs
ruled_out.blocked_by: Forge test confirms mulDiv(max,max,max) = max. 512-bit CRT algorithm handles phantom overflow correctly. Halmos symbolic check (check_mulDivNoPhantomOverflow) explored 10+ paths, no counterexample found.
ruled_out.verdict: skip — correct implementation, no phantom overflow

ruled_out.blocked_by: Fuzz test (10000 runs) confirms mulDivRoundingUp >= mulDiv for all tested inputs and difference is at most 1. Halmos check_roundingUpAlwaysGtOrEq passed (13 paths explored).

ruled_out.hypothesis: C11: getNextSqrtPriceFromInput moves price wrong direction
ruled_out.blocked_by: Forge fuzz (10000 runs): zeroForOne always decreases price, oneForZero always increases. Edge cases (amount=0, min/max price) all pass. Halmos check_priceMovesCorrectDirection explored 31 paths.
Fuzz test (10000 runs): roundUp >= roundDown for all inputs. Same prices return 0. Max liquidity does not overflow for small price ranges. Halmos check_deltaRoundingDirection explored 65 paths.
Forge fuzz: total cost (amountIn + feeAmount) never exceeds input for 10000 random inputs. Edge cases: amountRemaining=1 with 30% fee gives 0 output, fee=0 gives 0 fee, fee=9999 takes nearly all.

Forge: round-trip tested at every 1000th tick from -887000 to 887000 (1775 ticks). Recovered tick is always tick or tick-1. MIN_TICK->MIN_SQRT_RATIO and MAX_TICK->MAX_SQRT_RATIO exact. Fuzz (10000 runs) confirms monotonicity.

ruled_out.hypothesis: C15: BitMath.mostSignificantBit incorrect for power of 2
ruled_out.blocked_by: Forge: MSB(2^n) == n for all n in [0,254]. LSB(2^n) == n for all n. MSB(0) reverts. MSB(1)=0. MSB(max)=255. Fuzz: MSB >= LSB always. Halmos check_msbOfPowerOf2 PASSED (3 paths, complete).
Forge: addDelta(50, -51) reverts. addDelta(max, 1) reverts. addDelta(max-1, 1) = max. addDelta(x, 0) = x for all x. Fuzz (10000 runs): correctly reverts on underflow and overflow.

ruled_out.hypothesis: C17: FeeHelper fee exceeds input or creates tokens
ruled_out.blocked_by: Forge: fee=0 returns 0, fee=10000 takes all (input), fee>10000 reverts. Output fee at 10000 reverts (>= check). Fuzz (10000 runs): fee + protocol never exceeds input. Halmos check_feeNeverExceedsInput, check_feeConservation explored.
ruled_out.verdict: skip — fee calculations conservative and correct

ruled_out.hypothesis: C18: CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput maker overpaid via rounding
ruled_out.blocked_by: CONFIRMED: CLOB rounds UP output (mulDivRoundingUp x2) while SingleProviderPool rounds DOWN (mulDiv x2). At non-integer prices, taker receives up to 2 extra wei per fill. Over 10000 1-wei fills at sqrt(2)*Q96 price, CLOB gives significantly more than pool. However: (1) each fill costs gas >> 2 wei value, (2) bounded at 2 wei per trade, (3) maker voluntarily placed the order. Economic impact: negligible (Tier C at best).
ruled_out.verdict: skip — rounding favors taker by max 2 wei, not economically exploitable

ruled_out.blocked_by: Forge: both-zero returns Q96, amount1=0 returns MIN_SQRT_RATIO, amount0=0 returns MAX_SQRT_RATIO. Max inputs don't overflow (dynamic scaling with maxMultiplier). Equal max amounts produce nonzero result.

Fuzz (10000 runs): calculateFixedInput rounds DOWN (mulDiv), calculateFixedOutput rounds UP (mulDivRoundingUp). Round-trip A->B->A always loses: amountBack <= amount for all prices and directions. No profitable round-trip path exists.

ruled_out.hypothesis: C23/INV-SW02: Profitable round-trip in any pool type
ruled_out.blocked_by: Forge fuzz at 10000 runs: Dynamic pool (SwapMath level) — no profit. Fixed pool (ratio swap level) — no profit. Fixed pool with fees — no profit. Fixed pool asymmetric ratios — no profit. SingleProvider — no profit. 25 separate test functions, all pass.
ruled_out.verdict: skip — no profitable round-trip in any pool type

ruled_out.hypothesis: C24/INV-SW03: Pool balance decreases from sequential 1-wei swaps
ruled_out.blocked_by: Forge: 100 sequential 1-wei swaps at 30% fee on DynamicPool: all produce 0 output (fee consumes entire 1 wei). Fixed pool invariant tests (10000 fuzz runs) confirm rounding always favors protocol.
ruled_out.verdict: skip — rounding favors protocol in all pool types

ruled_out.hypothesis: C25/INV-E01: Fee growth not monotonically non-decreasing
ruled_out.blocked_by: Integration tests verify feeGrowthGlobal is monotonically non-decreasing across 100 random swaps. InvariantLiquidityAccounting.t.sol assertion passes. Fee is added via += in _crossTick and computeSwap.
